name: openbot
description: LAF Agent — 사장님을 위한 일 시키는 봇. Always-on cloud Bots for Korean small businesses: each starts blank, works on a real browser with your logins, and every action is decided before it happens and recorded after. Fork of CopilotKit/OpenBot.

paragraphs: A Bot you can hand real work to, and actually trust with the access. It starts knowing nothing and becomes whatever you tell it. It works on a real browser with your logins, and every action it takes is decided before it happens and recorded after.
Quick start · What we changed · Features · Architecture · Docs

Give your Bot a name, tell it what you want, and it writes down what it is for. Watch it work on its own screen, type a password into a masked box it never sees when it asks for one, and teach it a task in words — kept as something you can ask for by name.
features: One computer per account: the Bot works on your computer — its files, its logins, its browser sessions. On an older account with several Bots they all share it; Bots are not a security boundary, the gateway in front of…

The gateway is the only way in: it resolves the target from a server-held snapshot, evaluates the policy, writes the audit row, and only then calls the computer. There is no path that acts without the record existing…

CEL policy, fail closed: rules can inspect tool.name, intent, bot.id, actor.id, page.url, page.host, element., key, submit, file., mcp. and repeat.count. Deny is evaluated before allow, a missing policy permits nothing,…

Nobody drives the Bot's browser: a person watches its screen, on every surface, and never clicks or types on it. A value the page needs — an ID, a password, a one-time code — goes into a masked box the Bot opens and…
Secrets never enter the transcript: the trail records that a secret was requested and how long it was, not what it said.

whatItDoes.text: A Bot you can hand real work to, and actually trust with the access. It starts knowing nothing and becomes whatever you tell it. It works on a real browser with your logins, and every action it takes is decided before it happens and recorded after.

requirements.text: Something only a person can do away from that screen, such as approving a sign-in on a phone, is asked for in the conversation and answered with 다 했어요 (computer.helprequested, computer.controlreleased).

AUTHPROVIDERS is what the sign-in buttons are drawn from — the server publishes it on GET /api/auth/providers and the screen asks before it draws — so it must agree with the credentials: a name with no credentials, or credentials nobody declared, stops the server rather than serving a button that posts into an error.
